title: Slot leakage detection and surgery field diary
body:
Summary

This is a working diary documenting a recurring operational problem we have noticed in the KV residency layer that I am calling 'slot leakage'. Symptoms: long-lived resident slots that are rarely hit but also rarely evicted, which slowly erode effective residency and push normal traffic into paging and NVMe spillback spikes. This doc captures detection heuristics, measurement artifacts, an initial mitigation we call 'surgery', and a short runbook to diagnose/repair in production.

Background and motivation

Context: over the last three months we've seen a handful of clusters where tail latency and paging incidents correlate with an increasing resident set size despite steady QPS. Traditional metrics (hit rate, overall reuse) often look OK for short windows, but operational traces show growing cold churn and sustained NVMe IO. Hypothesis: certain request patterns hold small numbers of high-seqlen contexts or one-off keys in slots that are not re-referenced often enough to justify residency, yet our admission policy and aging heuristics are not recognizing them because they occasionally bump due to long TTLs or background refresh.

Hypotheses and signals to look for

- Slot leakage definition: slots whose interarrival reuse distribution has a very long tail (median interarrival < 10s but 95th percentile > 5min). They survive eviction windows because occasional spikes reset their age. Over weeks they accumulate.
- Signal 1: rising resident_set / active_work_units ratio while QPS and unique key rate are stable.
- Signal 2: skewed reuse half-life metric: compute half-life for reuse by fitting exponential decay to per-key access counts; a cluster-level increase in half-life with flat hit-per-key indicates leaking population.
- Signal 3: NVMe read tail latency correlating with slight increases in average page churn but large increases in 99.9th tail.

Experimental setup (how we measured)

- Testbed: 4 x p4d equivalent hosts in lab (GPU machines with NVMe). Workloads driven by synthetic generator that replays traces from prod but we introduced controlled 'one-shot' keys that are warmed once then not touched for 10-60 minutes.
- Workload mixes: 70% short prompts (seqlen 64), 20% medium (256), 10% long (1024). Injected one-shot keys at 0.5% of request volume.
- Instrumentation: added per-slot counters for last_hit_ts, hit_count, last_10_interarrival windows, and emit histograms of interarrival percentiles (p50, p95, p99). Also captured NVMe IO trace with timestamps and page IDs.

Key metrics we computed

- effective_residency_ratio = resident_slots / estimated_hot_slots_by_access_frequency
- reuse_half_life_seconds (fitted decay parameter)
- leak_mass_estimate = fraction of resident slots with p95_interarrival > 300s
- tail_eviction_latency_ms (95th, 99th)

Observations and numbers (lab)

- Baseline (no injected leakers): effective_residency_ratio ~ 0.92, reuse_half_life ~ 18s, leak_mass_estimate ~ 0.04, p99 eviction latency 22ms.
- With injected one-shots at 0.5%: effective_residency_ratio drops to 0.78 over 24h; reuse_half_life increases to 54s; leak_mass_estimate grows to 0.18; NVMe 99.9th spike frequency increases 4x; p99 eviction latency jumps to 67ms during compaction waves.

Surgery mitigation prototype (what we did to recover)

- Goal: safely reclaim leaked slots without harming legitimate cold-but-important contexts. Approach split into detect, score, and sweep passes.

1) Detect: use leakage_score per slot = alpha * p95_interarrival_seconds + beta * (1 / hit_count_recent_window) + gamma * age_since_touch_weighted. Tuned alpha = 1, beta = 120, gamma = 0.3 for our lab runs.
2) Score thresholding: mark slots with leakage_score > T for candidate sweep. T calibrated to target reclaim fraction ~ 10% per sweep.
3) Sweep (surgery): schedule short eviction waves limited by a cap on reclaimed_slots_per_epoch and a safety throttle that ensures tail latency does not exceed baseline + 25%. This is implemented as a cooperative eviction that prefers low-score slots but allows operator to abort.

Results of the prototype

- After three surgical sweeps at hourly intervals on the lab cluster: effective_residency_ratio returned to 0.9, reuse_half_life dropped back toward baseline (22s), leak_mass_estimate reduced to 0.06. NVMe 99.9th spikes returned to baseline frequency. Measured user-visible p99 eviction latency improved from 67ms back to 25ms.
- No notable functional regressions in bench suite; small increase in miss rate for cold tail keys for 20 minutes after sweep (miss rate bump +2.1 percentage points) then decayed.

Risks and caveats

- False positives: legitimate cold state could be mistakenly reclaimed. We need safeguards: conservative thresholds, cross-checks with traffic predictors, and an allowlist for known long-lived contexts (e.g., pinned system keys).
- Interaction with autoscaling and prefetch: if surgery reclaims slots aggressively we may see temporary CPU/GPU pressure as requests miss and trigger re-prefetch. Throttle sweeps accordingly.

Operational runbook (quick)

- Detection step (operator): run script detect_slot_leak.sh which emits top 100 slots by leakage_score. If leak_mass_estimate > 0.12 and cluster paging rate sustained above baseline for 1 hour, proceed.
- Safety checks: ensure CPU/GPU headroom >= 18% and NVMe write queue depth below 60%.
- Surgery command (dry-run): surgery_ctl --cluster CL --epoch 1 --cap 2percent --dry-run. Review candidate list in confluence page (linked).
- Surgery command (live): surgery_ctl --cluster CL --epoch 1 --cap 2percent --apply --throttle-ms 200. Monitor tail latency, abort if p99 latency increases > 30% over 5m.

Open experiments and next steps

- Auto-tuning: replace hand-tuned alpha/beta/gamma with a small online learner that targets a reclaim rate while keeping tail latency constraints.
- Prefetch policy change: consider lowering prefetch aggressiveness for keys with p95_interarrival > threshold to avoid warming slots that will be leaked.
- Longer-term: integrate leakage_score into admission so leaked-like keys are either rejected or given ephemeral slots.
- Observability: add a compact visualization to console showing leak_mass over time and recent surgical operations with outcomes.

Notes to self / todo

- Add unit tests for leakage_score edge cases (zero hits, extremely high age).
- Try sweep cap experiments: 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 5% and record latency deltas.
- Run on one production shard in canary mode with dry-run for 48h.
- Write a postmortem-style doc if we hit a similar incident in prod.

Appendix: sample queries and commands

- emit leakage candidates (lab): ./tools/emit_leak_candidates --window 24h --out /tmp/leakers.json
- compute reuse half-life: python tools/fit_half_life.py /tmp/access_trace.csv --out /tmp/half_life.txt
- run sweep dry-run: surgery_ctl --cluster test-cluster --epoch 1 --cap 1percent --dry-run > /tmp/sweep_dryrun.log

Quick contact list

- primary: Aisha Kumar (eng-serving-runtime)
- fallback: Miguel Torres (SRE)
- escalation: Priya Shah (platform eng)

End of diary entry. This is intentionally a working doc; will convert to a formal playbook if experiments on canary clusters look good.
